question.text: A geostationary satellite is orbiting around an arbitrary planet <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>P</mi></math> at a height of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>11</mn><mi>R</mi></math> above the surface of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>P</mi></math>, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>R</mi></math> being the radius of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>P</mi></math>. The time period of another satellite in hours at a height of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn><mi>R</mi></math> from the surface of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>P</mi></math> is ________ has the time period of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>24</mn><mo> </mo><mi>hours</mi><mo>.</mo></math>
